title: Mastering Modern Layouts
subtitle: A Comprehensive Guide to CSS Flexbox

title: Introducing Flexbox
bullets: Flexbox is a powerful one-dimensional layout model.
It simplifies the alignment and distribution of space among items.
Ideal for building responsive and dynamic user interfaces.

title: The Flex Container
body:
To utilize Flexbox, you first need to define a flex container. This is achieved by applying the 'display: flex' or 'display: inline-flex' property to an HTML element. 

This declaration transforms the element into a flex container, enabling you to control the layout of its direct children, known as flex items.

title: Creating a Container
description: This code snippet demonstrates how to create a flex container.

title: Flex Items and Main Axis
body:
Direct children of a flex container automatically become flex items. These items are laid out along either the main axis or the cross axis, depending on the 'flex-direction' property. 

By default, the main axis is horizontal (row), and the cross axis is vertical (column).  Understanding these axes is crucial for controlling item arrangement.

title: Item Ordering
description: The 'order' property allows you to rearrange flex items.

title: The 'flex-direction' Property
body:
The 'flex-direction' property determines the direction of the main axis. It can take on four values: 'row', 'column', 'row-reverse', and 'column-reverse'. 

'row' (default) arranges items horizontally, while 'column' arranges them vertically. The 'reverse' options invert the direction of the main axis.

title: Changing Direction
description: This example demonstrates how to use 'flex-direction: column'.

title: Summary
bullets: Flexbox utilizes a flex container and flex items.
The 'flex-direction' property controls the main axis.

title: Controlling Item Alignment
bullets: Flexbox provides powerful tools for aligning items.
These properties control alignment along main and cross axes.

title: 'justify-content' Property
body:
The 'justify-content' property defines alignment along the main axis. Common values include 'flex-start', 'flex-end', 'center', 'space-between', and 'space-around'.

'flex-start' aligns items to the beginning, 'flex-end' to the end, and 'center' in the middle. 'space-between' distributes space evenly between items, while 'space-around' adds space around each item.

title: Justify Content Example
'align-items' Property
body:
The 'align-items' property controls alignment along the cross axis.  Values include 'stretch', 'flex-start', 'flex-end', 'center', and 'baseline'.

'stretch' (default) stretches items to fill the container.  Other values align items to the start, end, or center of the cross axis.

title: Align Items Example
The 'align-content' Property
body:
When multiple lines of flex items exist (due to 'flex-wrap: wrap'), 'align-content' controls the alignment of these lines along the cross axis.  

Values mirror those of 'justify-content': 'flex-start', 'flex-end', 'center', 'space-between', and 'space-around'. It impacts how lines are distributed within the container.

title: Align Content Example
Summary
bullets: 'justify-content' aligns items on the main axis.
'align-items' aligns items on the cross axis.

title: Flex Item Properties
bullets: Flex items have properties for size and spacing.
These properties provide fine-grained control over item behavior.

title: The 'flex-basis' Property
body:
The 'flex-basis' property specifies the initial main size of a flex item. It determines how much space the item will occupy before any available space is distributed. 

If set to 'auto', the item's size is based on its content.  It's considered alongside 'flex-grow' and 'flex-shrink' to calculate the final size.

title: Setting Flex Basis
description: Demonstrates different values for the 'flex-basis' property.

title: 'flex-grow' and 'flex-shrink'
body:
The 'flex-grow' property defines how much the item will grow relative to other flex items if there is available space. A higher value means it will grow more. 

Conversely, 'flex-shrink' specifies how much the item will shrink relative to others if there isn't enough space.  A higher value means it will shrink more readily.

title: Grow and Shrink
The 'flex' Shorthand
body:
The 'flex' property is a shorthand for 'flex-grow', 'flex-shrink', and 'flex-basis'.  It allows you to set all three values in a single declaration. 

The order is: 'flex-grow flex-shrink flex-basis'.  A common value is '1', which means grow to fill available space, shrink if needed, and have an initial size based on content.

title: Using the Flex Shorthand
description: Demonstrates how to use the 'flex' shorthand property.

title: Summary
bullets: 'flex-basis' defines the initial size of an item.
'flex-grow' controls how much an item grows.
'flex-shrink' controls how much an item shrinks.
The 'flex' shorthand combines all three properties.
